spots.name: Golden Bridge
spots.label: Golden Bridge

text.access_note: This is inside the Sun World Ba Na Hills park, so an entry ticket is needed; check the official site before you go for tickets, hours and closures.
text.directions_text: No Underground, train or tram stops are listed for this spot, so make your way from central Da Nang to Sun World Ba Na Hills. In Google Maps you may need to search for "Sun World Ba Na Hills" rather than the bridge name. Once inside, the bridge is reached only by cable car. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.
text.geographic_location: The bridge is in the Bà Nà Hills resort in Hòa Vang district, Da Nang, and joins the cable car station to the gardens.
text.description:
The Golden Bridge (Cầu Vàng) is a pedestrian walkway in the Bà Nà Hills resort, in Hòa Vang district. It is about 150 metres long and curves almost back on itself. Two giant hands, built from fibreglass and wire mesh to look like stone, seem to hold it up. It was built to link the cable car station with the gardens, and it also works as a lookout. Construction began in July 2017 and finished in April 2018, and the bridge opened in June 2018.

The best-known photos are taken on the bridge, but this map's stand-here point is at Chùa Linh Ứng, in the pagoda grounds near the bridge area. From here you see the whole bridge from a distance, across the valley, with mountains and prayer flags in the scene. It is also usually quieter than the bridge, and one visitor found it nearly empty during a 30-minute stay.

The bridge looks small from this far away, so use your phone's zoom lens and let the valley and the flags give the picture scale. Fog often covers the view, so a clear day makes a big difference. If you want a close, upward shot of the stone hands, Cầu Vàng itself gives that view, and Le Jardin D'Amour shows the bridge arching overhead.

shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand at Chùa Linh Ứng (pagoda grounds near the Golden Bridge area). The bridge seen from a distance across the valley, with mountains and prayer flags in the scene. From there the bridge lies to the south-east, seen from a distance across the valley, with mountains and prayer flags around it.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and put the bridge on one of the lines, not in the centre. Let prayer flags or the valley fill the foreground so the bridge has some scale. Take one wide shot at 1x, then a closer one with the telephoto. For a different angle, Le Jardin D'Amour has the bridge arching overhead with the stone hands and flower beds in front.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the bridge to set focus, then slide the exposure down a little so the sky does not turn white. If mist drifts through, take a few shots a minute apart. A panorama can capture the whole valley, but hold the phone steady while it sweeps. Drones are not permitted.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Go on a clear day and take the first cable car, around 7:00 to 8:00 AM, because fog often covers the view later. Check opening hours and any closures before your visit.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Use telephoto (2x to 5x, depending on your phone) to bring the bridge closer across the valley. The default lens (1x) is better for the wider scene with the mountains and prayer flags. Try the ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you want a flag or the pagoda grounds large in the foreground.

spots.alt: Golden Bridge, Da Nang: a pedestrian walkway in the Bà Nà Hills resort, in Hòa Vang district. Photo spot

spots.name: Marble Mountains
spots.label: Marble Mountains

text.access_note: This is a visited religious and heritage site with pagodas and shrines, and parts of it may be ticketed or restricted, so check the official site before you go.
text.directions_text: From central Da Nang, head south towards Ngũ Hành Sơn District by taxi or hired scooter. Ask for Thủy Sơn and Tam Thai Pagoda. From the pagoda, climb the steps up the west side of Thủy Sơn to Vọng Giang Đài. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.
text.geographic_location: The Marble Mountains are in Ngũ Hành Sơn District, south of Da Nang city, near Non Nuoc Beach. The five hills stand together as a small cluster of rock. The Co Co River is visible behind them in the view from the pavilion.
text.description:
The Marble Mountains, also called Ngũ Hành Sơn or 'five elements mountains', are a cluster of five marble and limestone hills just south of Da Nang city. Each hill is named after an element: metal, water, wood, fire and earth. They rise sharply out of flat land close to the coast, so they stand out in any wide view. Thủy Sơn is the one visitors can climb. Its 156 steps lead to a summit with wide views, and its caves and Buddhist and Hindu shrines hold carved statues and reliefs.

The best-known photo is taken from Vọng Giang Đài, a stone pavilion on the west side of Thủy Sơn. From the pavilion you look back over all five hills together, with Non Nuoc Beach, the Co Co River and the Da Nang skyline behind them. Guides treat it as the main viewpoint, and it is the one place where all five hills fit into a single frame.

The area is also known for stone carving, and the mountains were given National Special Relic status in January 2019. If you have time, two other spots are worth a look. Động Huyền Không is a cave where a shaft of daylight falls through the roof onto the altar and statues. The highest point, Đỉnh Thượng Thái, looks east over the coast. Take the pavilion photo first, while the light is soft, then explore the caves.

shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Vọng Giang Đài (west side of Thủy Sơn, reached by the steps from Tam Thai Pagoda). From the stone pavilion you look back over the five marble hills together, with Non Nuoc Beach, the Co Co River and the Da Nang skyline behind them. The stone pavilion on the west side of Thủy Sơn, reached by the steps from Tam Thai Pagoda. From the pavilion you look back over the five marble hills, with Non Nuoc Beach, the Co Co River and the Da Nang skyline behind them.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the line of hills on the lower third, so the sky and skyline fill the rest. Include a corner of the pavilion's stone edge in the foreground to add depth. If you go on to Động Huyền Không, shoot the beam of light falling on the altar and statues, with the incense smoke in it. Hold the phone steady and ask before photographing monks or altars.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the hills to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so the sky keeps its colour. In the dim cave, tap on the lit altar and lower the exposure so the beam doesn't blow out. Night mode may kick in in dark corners, so keep your hands still.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Sunrise or sunset, when the light is warm and soft. Check the official site before you go, as the site closes in the late afternoon and sunset may fall after closing.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) at the pavilion, so all five hills and the skyline fit in one frame. Switch to the default lens (1x) for a more natural look, and use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out a single hill or the beach.

spots.alt: Marble Mountains, Da Nang: a cluster of five marble and limestone hills just south. Photo spot

text.access_note: This is a stretch of public beach with no payment needed; mind the warning flags because of rip currents, and check local rules before flying a drone.
text.directions_text: There are no public transport stops at this spot; get to Võ Nguyên Giáp street, near the Fusion Maia resort entrance, by your own means. Then walk onto the beach in front of the street. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.
text.geographic_location: My Khe Beach is a city beach in Da Nang with the open sea beyond the shore, and Son Tra Peninsula is visible in the distance. The stretch for this photo lies in front of Võ Nguyên Giáp street, near the Fusion Maia resort entrance.
text.description: My Khe is a long city beach in Da Nang, and it works well for phone photos because the scene is simple: sand, sea and a wide sky. The best frame is at sunrise. The light is low and golden on the wet sand, and basket boats and fishermen are often on the shore with the open sea behind them. A local photography guide describes sunrise as the one-hour window for shooting My Khe. The stretch in front of Võ Nguyên Giáp street is said to be less crowded than the hotel section further north. If you want a different kind of picture, the palm-lined pavements along the same street make good frames for portraits of your travelling companions. Aim to arrive a little before the light changes, so you have time to walk down to the sand and look for a boat or a figure to give the picture a focus. One guide says the beach is busier in the late afternoon, so early morning gives you the calmest scene. Keep an eye on the flags, as rip currents occur here, and stay out of the water while you are concentrating on your screen.

shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Võ Nguyên Giáp (beach stretch in front of the street, near the Fusion Maia resort entrance). Low, golden sunrise light on wet sand, with basket boats and fishermen on the shore and the open sea beyond. Near the Fusion Maia resort entrance.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the horizon on the upper or lower line so it stays level. Keep a boat or fisherman in the foreground to give the scene scale. For portraits, try portrait mode against the palm-lined pavements along the street. As an alternative, from the beach itself (Bãi biển Mỹ Khê), Son Tra Peninsula rises in the distance with the Lady Buddha statue visible on the mountain, and Công viên Biển Đông has the carp-turned-dragon statue against the sea.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the brightest part of the sky to focus, then slide the exposure down a little so the sunrise colours stay rich. Use night mode only if it is still quite dark, and hold the phone steady against your body. Take a Live Photo to catch boats moving on the shore.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: About 5:45 AM from November to March, before the boats leave around 6:30 AM.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for a natural view of the boats, the wet sand and the sea. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) for the full sweep of the shore. Use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out a fisherman or a single boat.
